findings.title: Replace the local link before publishing `vite-plus`.
findings.comment:
**Replace the local link before publishing `vite-plus`.**

The `link:../../../tsgo-effect` dependency works only while the sibling package exists at that repository path. A published `vite-plus` package does not contain that sibling, so consumers cannot resolve this dependency from the published manifest. Use a registry version for the published dependency and arrange local linking separately. pnpm documents publication-time conversion for `workspace:` dependencies, not this `link:` dependency. ([pnpm.io](https://pnpm.io/fr/11.x/workspaces?utm_source=openai))
findings.reason: The changed nested vite-plus manifest is a source-development dependency, outside the root eight-package workspace and root publication selection. The repository publishes packages/vite-plus as @tiara-stack/vite-plus. scripts/sync-vite-plus.mjs:58-60 unconditionally writes the published tsgo dependency to ^0.1.2 and the checked public manifest has that registry range. scripts/check-vite-plus-package.mjs:16 asserts that exact value. Root build, check:vite-plus and public-package dry pack passed on the same source epoch. Direct publication of the raw upstream source checkout is outside this repository release contract. Replacing this local-source integration with a registry dependency would violate the authorized workspace-source development requirement.

findings.title: Propagate Effect diagnostic failures from both workers.
findings.comment:
**Propagate Effect diagnostic failures from both workers.**

If `effectlint.RunSelected` returns an error, these branches stop their worker without reporting the error. `RunLinterOnProgram` can then return nil even though the worker did not lint its remaining files. Collect worker errors and return one to the caller.   


Also applies to: 589-589
findings.reason: The two silent returns are present in exact assigned main. More decisively, the current Effect runner returns an error only when selectRules receives an unknown Effect rule name. effectlint.All validates all 82 fixed names against effectrules.All at initialization, effectNameByHeadlessName is built from that validated set, SelectedRuleNames filters other linter names, and RunSelected ignores unknown headless names before invoking the runner with one validated Effect name. The current internal registry is static; no supported input can pass an unknown name through this adapter. Context cancellation is not an error return from this runner. Tests assert the 82 names exist. The ticket does not introduce or materially increase a reachable dropped-error condition. Error propagation would be useful if a later runner introduces real fallible operations, at which point this boundary must change with it.

findings.title: Correct the Effect lint base identities in this carry packet.
findings.comment:
**Correct the Effect lint base identities in this carry packet.**

`40-carry-02.paths.part-03.json` marks `effectlint.go` and `effectlint_test.go` as additions with `"before": null`. `41-candidate-dispositions.json` records non-null base hashes for both paths under the same source base and head. Reconcile the base files and regenerate these entries so reviewers can assess the adapter changes.
findings.reason: The finding conflates two explicitly distinct refs. Each carry index declares both source_base (actual assigned main cf6cd57) and projection_base (the pinned upstream reconstruction used to exclude stock imports). Entry before/after modes and blobs describe the declared projection base/head; before:null is correct because neither Tiara Effect adapter file exists in pinned upstream/reconstructed base fed1b7f3. The disposition evidence separately hashes files already present in actual main to assess preexisting behavior. Both assertions are verified by direct Git object reads and agree with the custom-addition source ledger. Replacing the projection preimages with actual-main hashes would corrupt the approved upstream/custom reconstruction; no mapping correction is warranted.

findings.reviewer_claim_confirmed: The source-binary/override lookup shape is duplicated. No duplication or potential future maintenance drift is denied. A per-package shared plain-JavaScript helper is possible without a cross-package dependency.
findings.reason: This is the installed skill's explicitly discretionary smell baseline, not a documented-standard breach or demonstrated current behavior failure. The package intentionally ships an unbuilt plain Node CLI and a separately bundled typed API. Independent entrypoint resolvers already existed on actual main; the bounded API fix restores their source/installed selection parity. Consolidation would add a shared shipped runtime asset and change the build/entrypoint dependency boundary for a maintenance-only benefit. The existing parameterized regression cases cover both tools and both entrypoints for local source, overrides, missing local builds and installed optional-platform resolution; packed vendor CLI/API and TypeScript5.9 consumers also pass. For this baseline-alignment change, retaining the self-contained entrypoints with those parity guards is a reasonable tradeoff. The raw low-priority recommendation is preserved for later resolver-design work, rather than treated as a mandatory correctness repair.
